analysis.title: Tech takes the strain: Will key supports hold?
key_insights: The S&P 500 fell 1.75% in October, but leadership split sharply: Technology -10.16% and Consumer Discretionary -9.45%, versus Energy +11.46%, Healthcare +11.25% and Consumer Staples +11.04%.

Investors have grown more cautious on the AI trade, with scrutiny of heavy corporate capex and uncertain near-term monetisation pressuring the Mag-7 and Semiconductors, the two main drivers of Nasdaq 100 and S&P 500 gains.

A positioning squeeze in the leadership areas over the past month pushed capital toward defensive segments. The key question into year-end is whether this is a durable rotation away from growth or a concentrated unwind that allows a tactical rebound.

The Nasdaq 100 slipped into correction and fell to just above its rising 200-day SMA at 27,940. The RSI is testing long-term support near oversold. A close below the 200-day SMA exposes 27,176-26,182.
A Nasdaq 100 recovery above 28,750 would preserve the lower-degree wave-5 scenario toward 31,650, then an extended objective near 34,419.

The SOX index is still up 57% year to date despite last week's sell-off. SOXL hit an all-time high at 302 and then consolidated sharply, with a possible final leg lower toward 59-52 while it stays capped at 125 on rebounds. An RSI bullish divergence suggests downside momentum is fading.

The Mag-7 are almost 35% of the S&P 500. Since the start of October they lost about USD 1,500bn in market cap while the other 493 stocks added USD 217bn, and the S&P 500 shed about USD 1,268bn over the past month.

Five Mag-7 members have reported (Alphabet, Tesla, Meta, Amazon, Microsoft). Reactions were severe where results missed or guidance fell short. Over the past month Alphabet is -19%, Meta -15% and Nvidia -13%, while Tesla is +7% and Apple +3%.

The Bloomberg Magnificent Seven Index validated a head and shoulders pattern with a downside target near 33,000. A final leg lower toward 32,600-32,750 is possible, where the broader bullish trend could resume. The index remains in a bullish medium-term structure with no RSI divergence yet.
Apple is at the 350 wave-5 target. It stays constructive above 326-310, with scope for 350 and then 415. Below 326-310, focus shifts to 260.
Nvidia reached a standard wave-5 target at 243. A break of the ascending support line plus an RSI break points to deeper consolidation, with support at 190-184.

Microsoft is constructive after a double-bottom trigger, with an upside target of 583 above the prior all-time high of 555. Support is at 505 (23.6% Fibonacci, near the 50-day SMA), and 470 is the fallback base toward 583 and potentially 693.

Alphabet broke several supports and fell toward 274-260, the 50% Fibonacci retracement and the triangle's projected downside target. Rebounds are capped at 329-310 and bearish pressure is likely to persist. The long-term structure stays bullish above 203.
Meta has traded in a triangle since its late-2025 high and is moving toward 585-555 at the lower boundary, where stabilisation could emerge. The RSI break points to near-term weakness.

Amazon broke below its 200-day SMA and approached 230-220 support (61.8% and 76.4% Fibonacci retracements, rising support line since 2023). Bearish pressure persists while capped by resistance at 250.
Tesla broke above the falling resistance in place since the start of the year, with the RSI confirming. The first target is 450, ahead of the prior all-time high at 500.
Pictet frames the correction as a structural reset in the main growth engines rather than broad capitulation, and expects choppy price action until support zones are tested.

Historical study: the Nasdaq-100 closed 9.1% below its all-time high after a 3.46% one-day drop, still above its 200-day average at 27,927. This is the 21st occurrence since 1990 of the setup (more than 9% below the high, above the 200-day, down at least 1% on the day). At least 70% of outcomes were positive from day 10 onward, with average forward returns near 5% after 25 days.
Cited risks: reassessment of AI and semiconductor capex expectations, rotation to defensives, and event risk around big tech earnings, the US midterms and the Gulf conflict.

tension_points.bull_case: Historical analogues of the Nasdaq-100 drawdown setup show at least 70% positive outcomes from day 10 onward and average returns near 5% after 25 days. The report calls the move a structural reset rather than capitulation, with the long-term uptrend intact in Mag-7 names such as Microsoft and Apple.
tension_points.bear_case: Investors are reassessing AI and semiconductor capex, capital is rotating to defensives, and several mega-caps are still moving toward key support. Alphabet, Amazon and Meta show negative RSI signals.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A close below the Nasdaq 100's 200-day SMA at 27,940 would expose 27,176-26,182.

tension_points.bull_case: The index stays in a bullish medium-term structure with no RSI divergence yet, and a final leg lower toward 32,600-32,750 could let the broader bullish trend resume.
